answer: TPM-bound attestation gates admission: a fused Endorsement Key's private half never leaves the die, each login signs a quote over boot registers and a monotonic counter. Faking N identities buys N TPM chips at eight dollars each, each with a CA-signed EK certificate. No cloning: the private half is non-exportable. No bulk-minting: each certificate needs a die and foundry signature. No replay: the counter advances. Detected clusters lose EK certificates and every anchored identity is slashed. Like a beacon on a dark ocean, only keys forged in the silicon kernel stay lit while fakes sink.
